title: People Would Pay 'Male' AI Agents More, Study Finds
paragraphs: AI agents are increasingly being used in workplaces, sometimes being treated more like co-workers than just digital tools.
A study looked at how much people would pay them for their work, and the results found an unexpected gender gap.
The study asked 189 participants — 115 men and 74 women — to wear VR headsets and work with an AI agent to complete tasks in a virtual workspace.
In the VR world, the AI agent was depicted in one of three ways.
One agent looked like a text-based chatbot on a virtual computer screen. Another looked like a small humanoid robot standing on the participant's desk.
And the third looked like a human sitting in a chair beside the participant. These "human-like" agents could either appear as male named Johan, or female called Johanna.
After completing the tasks, the participants evaluated the quality of their AI assistant's work, and gave them credit for how much they helped.
Participants were also asked to divide a small payment of around $5 between them and the AI agent — and were told that any money given to the agent would be invested in its development.

Participants said they trusted Johan and Johanna's work more than the work of the other agents, and gave them more credit for helping — even though all the agents had the same underlying capabilities.
Johan and Johanna also got paid more than the other agents. However, even though the quality of their work was rated similarly, both male and female participants paid Johanna 10% less than Johan.

And it seems this wasn't done consciously. Because when the researchers interviewed 34 participants, 30 said they would trust and reward an AI assistant just as much regardless of its apparent gender.
And while Johan and Johanna were higher rated in the surveys, when interviewed, many participants said they preferred non-human-like assistants.
The researchers said this shows how people may not always be aware of their biases — and that researchers can't trust that users will actually react to AI the way they say they will.
